topic-144-a-connectionist-learning-contr.evolution: An early 1987 robot learns visual–joint mappings through action, and a 1992 practice strategy gradually increases trajectory difficulty. Later work studies attractor-based primitives and character control; recent methods emphasize morphological attention and actuator coordination. These examples share the use of structured representations, without implying that modern control guarantees apply to the earlier systems.
openQuestions: Which action representations transfer across changes in mechanical structure?
How can learned coordination retain control authority during unexpected contact?
topic-144-a-connectionist-learning-contr.overview: Motor learning connects desired movements with the dynamics of a body and its actuators. The represented work learns inverse dynamics, reusable movement primitives, adaptation to morphology, and low-dimensional coordination of many actuators. Physical continuity and body structure can make the learning problem easier than an unconstrained search over actions.
topic-144-a-connectionist-learning-contr.title: Motor Learning and Adaptive Embodied Control
topic-144-a-connectionist-learning-contr.whyItMatters: A controller must remain effective when speed, load, or body configuration changes. Useful representations can reduce the experience needed to learn coordinated behavior while retaining the ability to produce precise movements.

topic-145-a-kernel-perspective-on-distil.evolution: The representatives include educational skill discovery and machine teaching before and alongside modern neural distillation. Recent papers analyze whether distillation transfers the intended behavior and use context-conditioned teachers for continual language-model adaptation. This grouping connects learning from other learners, not a demonstrated historical dependency between tutoring models and neural compression.
openQuestions: How can teacher signals be matched to a student’s representational limits?
When does self-distillation denoise knowledge rather than progressively forget useful distinctions?
topic-145-a-kernel-perspective-on-distil.overview: Knowledge distillation trains one model using information supplied by another, but a more accurate teacher is not automatically a more useful teacher. The topic includes student-friendly representations, transfer between heterogeneous architectures, self-distillation, and retaining existing skills while incorporating new knowledge. A smaller educational strand studies how latent skills and teaching examples support learning.
topic-145-a-kernel-perspective-on-distil.title: Knowledge Transfer, Teaching, and Distillation
topic-145-a-kernel-perspective-on-distil.whyItMatters: Transfer quality depends on what the learner can represent and which signals the teacher exposes. Compression or adaptation can remove noise, but may also erase information needed for later tasks.

topic-146-a-back-propagation-algorithm-w.evolution: Late-1980s work explores temporal state representations and neural emission estimates for Markov models. The 1990s representatives refine hybrid recognition and feature extraction. Recent datasets and low-resource language-detection methods emphasize linguistic diversity, while a speech-first position paper argues for broader research priorities. These later concerns expand evaluation rather than erase the earlier temporal-modeling problem.
openQuestions: How can low-resource systems distinguish accent variation from a change of language?
Which acoustic representations preserve timing cues needed beyond transcription?
topic-146-a-back-propagation-algorithm-w.overview: Speech recognition maps changing acoustic signals to linguistic categories while coping with timing, speakers, accents, and limited data. This cluster strongly features early combinations of neural discriminators with hidden Markov models, where learned acoustic probabilities and structured temporal decoding perform different roles. Newer representatives revisit robustness and coverage of underserved speech varieties.
topic-146-a-back-propagation-algorithm-w.title: Neural Speech Recognition and Temporal Acoustic Modeling
topic-146-a-back-propagation-algorithm-w.whyItMatters: Better frame classification does not automatically improve whole-word recognition. A useful system must combine local evidence consistently over time and avoid cascading errors when an accent or language is unfamiliar.

topic-147-textdt-text2-decision-targeted.evolution: The historical span includes off-policy evaluation and later option learning. Around 2020–2022, representatives emphasize model-based offline optimization, stationary-distribution correction, and unsupervised pretraining. Recent work adds cross-domain value alignment and task-structured trajectory augmentation. The collection reflects several complementary ways to extract more value from fixed experience, each with its own coverage assumptions.
openQuestions: When does synthetic trajectory augmentation improve coverage without reinforcing model error?
Which representation objectives transfer across changes in reward or logging policy?
topic-147-textdt-text2-decision-targeted.overview: Offline reinforcement learning seeks useful policies from previously collected trajectories rather than unrestricted new interaction. The represented methods address policy optimization, value estimation, learned dynamics, and representations that make historical experience more useful. Dataset coverage and behavior quality shape which decisions the data can support.
topic-147-textdt-text2-decision-targeted.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning and Off-Policy Representation
topic-147-textdt-text2-decision-targeted.whyItMatters: A policy can exploit inaccurate value estimates in regions absent from the dataset. Reliable learning must distinguish genuine improvement from optimistic extrapolation, especially when combining experience from different sources or augmenting limited trajectories.

topic-148-a-bit-more-bayesian-domain-inv.evolution: A 2006 representative formalizes representation tradeoffs through generalization bounds. Later methods learn and co-regularize alignments, while 2019 theory supplies counterexamples to invariance-only reasoning. Recent work explores multi-source biomedical adaptation and synthetic noise domains. These extensions change the available supervision without eliminating the need to justify what transfers.
openQuestions: How can adaptation detect label or conditional shifts without enough target labels?
Which alignment objectives preserve useful distinctions across multiple target domains?
topic-148-a-bit-more-bayesian-domain-inv.overview: Domain adaptation transfers a predictor between distributions, often using source labels and little target supervision. Representations that make domains look similar are appealing, but may erase information needed to distinguish classes. The central question is which differences should be removed and which reflect genuine changes in the prediction problem.
topic-148-a-bit-more-bayesian-domain-inv.title: Domain Adaptation and the Limits of Invariance
topic-148-a-bit-more-bayesian-domain-inv.whyItMatters: Matching feature distributions alone does not guarantee target accuracy. Conditional shifts and different class proportions can make source performance and invariance compatible with poor transfer, so assumptions about the source–target relationship matter.

topic-149-a-dynamic-learning-strategy-fo.evolution: Earlier representatives model uncertainty in hidden variables and neural weights. Deep ensembles and dataset-shift evaluations become prominent in the late 2010s, followed by evidential and efficient single-model alternatives. Recent work revisits theoretical foundations and post-hoc estimation. The examples show continuing tradeoffs among calibration, interpretation, and cost rather than one universally superior uncertainty measure.
openQuestions: Which uncertainty estimates remain informative after the deployment distribution changes?
How should uncertainty be evaluated against the actual cost of downstream decisions?
topic-149-a-dynamic-learning-strategy-fo.overview: Uncertainty estimation asks whether a model knows how reliable its prediction is. Methods include distributions over weights, ensembles, evidential outputs, normalizing flows, and possibility-based formulations. They differ in what uncertainty means and how much additional computation is required to estimate it.
topic-149-a-dynamic-learning-strategy-fo.title: Predictive Uncertainty and Calibration
topic-149-a-dynamic-learning-strategy-fo.whyItMatters: A confident error under distribution shift can be more damaging than an acknowledged limitation. Useful uncertainty should support decisions about deferral, data collection, or human involvement, rather than merely producing a numerical confidence score.

topic-150-a-brain-machine-interface-oper.evolution: The 1996 representatives analyze temporal coding and rapid processing through asynchronous spikes. Later work develops more precise backpropagation over neuronal state and firing times. Recent methods add self-supervised visual learning, time-to-first-spike training, and joint weight-and-spike sparsification. These are different routes to useful temporal computation, not evidence that every spiking implementation is inherently faster or more efficient.
openQuestions: How can temporal learning reduce latency without discarding useful timing information?
Which reported efficiency gains survive deployment on realistic neuromorphic hardware?
topic-150-a-brain-machine-interface-oper.overview: Spiking networks represent information through discrete events and their timing. Training must handle discontinuous firing while controlling latency, spike count, and predictive accuracy. The represented work studies temporal gradients, information bottlenecks, conversion from conventional networks, and self-supervised representations suitable for event-driven computation.
topic-150-a-brain-machine-interface-oper.title: Spiking Neural Networks and Temporal Coding
topic-150-a-brain-machine-interface-oper.whyItMatters: Sparse activity can reduce energy on appropriate hardware, but an inefficient temporal code may require so many steps that savings disappear. Training quality and deployment efficiency therefore need to be assessed together.

topic-151-learning-by-instruction-in-con.evolution: Archival titles from the 1980s and 1990s concern concept induction, prior knowledge, analogy, and causality, but their missing abstracts limit detailed historical claims. The available 2026 evidence emphasizes modular cognitive representations and learned executable theories. This supports a thematic connection, not a verified chain of intellectual influence.
openQuestions: How can explanatory programs be tested against alternative theories with similar predictions?
What evidence validates a learned cognitive structure beyond downstream accuracy?
topic-151-learning-by-instruction-in-con.overview: This cluster connects learning concepts with constructing structured explanations of observations. The recent abstracts describe generative models of student cognitive structure and executable latent programs that explain how observed phenomena arise. The common ambition is a reusable representation of relationships, rather than a predictor tied only to one output label.
topic-151-learning-by-instruction-in-con.title: Concept Learning and Explicit Explanatory Structure
topic-151-learning-by-instruction-in-con.whyItMatters: Explicit structure can support interpretation and transfer when new tasks require recombining what was learned. However, a useful predictive representation is not automatically a faithful account of how a person thinks or how the world works.
